cloudflare_aaa_id_response: A webhook destination for Cloudflare's Notifications service. Defines the URL Cloudflare posts a notification payload to when a configured alert fires, with an optional shared secret sent in the `cf-webhook-auth` header so the receiving endpoint can verify the request originated from Cloudflare.
cloudflare_aaa_schemas_single_response: A webhook destination for Cloudflare's Notifications service, the same real concept as cloudflare_aaa_id_response discovered via a distinct read path in Cloudflare's own spec. Defines the URL and optional shared secret used to deliver notification payloads.
cloudflare_aaa_single_response: A notification policy in Cloudflare's Notifications (Alerting) service. Defines which event type triggers a notification (`alert_type`), any filters narrowing which events qualify, and the delivery mechanisms (e.g. email addresses, webhook destination IDs) notifications are dispatched to.
cloudflare_access_idp_federation_grant_r: Grants federation to an existing Cloudflare Access identity provider (`idp_id`), the mechanism by which an already-configured identity provider is included in Access's federated authentication flow.
cloudflare_access_policy_update_resp: Represents a test run of one or more Access policies against a simulated request. Used to check whether specific Access policies would allow or deny a given request without applying them for real.
cloudflare_access_single_response_10: An account-level Access policy. Defines the authentication and authorization rules (approval requirements, MFA configuration, browser isolation, session duration) applied to requests for the applications this policy is attached to.
cloudflare_access_single_response_11: A custom page for Cloudflare Access -- branded HTML shown to end users during the Access authentication flow (e.g. a custom login or blocked-access page), identified by its own `type` and referenceable by the applications it's assigned to.
cloudflare_access_single_response_14: An Access tag -- a label that can be attached to Access applications, used to group and filter applications in the Cloudflare dashboard and API.
cloudflare_access_single_response_17: A zone-level Access group. Defines a reusable set of Include/Exclude/Require authentication rules (matched against a user's identity, IP, device posture, etc.) that Access policies can reference by group instead of repeating the same rules.
cloudflare_access_single_response_18: A zone-level Access service token -- a non-interactive credential (client ID/secret pair) that lets a service authenticate to an Access-protected application without a human login. Supports secret rotation via `client_secret_version`, keeping the previous secret valid until `previous_client_secret_expires_at`.
cloudflare_access_single_response_2: An account-level Access service token, the same real concept as cloudflare_access_single_response_18 scoped to an account rather than a single zone -- a non-interactive credential letting a service authenticate to Access-protected applications, with rotation support via `client_secret_version`.
cloudflare_access_single_response_20: A zone-level Access mutual TLS (mTLS) certificate, used to authenticate client devices to Access-protected applications on the hostnames listed in `associated_hostnames`.
cloudflare_access_single_response_22: An Access policy scoped to a specific zone-level Access application. Defines the Include/Exclude/Require rules and the resulting `decision` (allow/deny/bypass) applied when a request matches, with `precedence` controlling evaluation order among the application's own policies.
cloudflare_access_single_response_4: An account-level Access group, the same real concept as cloudflare_access_single_response_17 scoped to an account rather than a single zone -- a reusable set of Include/Exclude/Require rules Access policies can reference by group.
cloudflare_access_single_response_6: An account-level Access mutual TLS (mTLS) certificate, the same real concept as cloudflare_access_single_response_20 scoped to an account rather than a single zone.
cloudflare_access_single_user_response: An Access user record for the account -- represents an individual who has authenticated through Access, identified by their email address.
cloudflare_addressing_full_response: An Address Map in Cloudflare's BYOIP (Bring Your Own IP) addressing service. Groups a set of IP addresses (`ips`) and assigns them to specific zones or the whole account (`memberships`) so Cloudflare's DNS responds with those IPs only for the assigned scope, once `enabled`.
cloudflare_addressing_single_response: An IP address prefix (BYOIP) registered with Cloudflare for advertisement under a given Autonomous System Number (`asn`). `loa_document_id` references the uploaded Letter of Authorization proving the account's right to advertise the prefix; `delegate_loa_creation` lets Cloudflare generate that document on the owner's behalf instead.
cloudflare_addressing_single_response_bg: A BGP-advertised sub-prefix of a parent BYOIP address prefix, identified by its own CIDR block. Represents a smaller range Cloudflare announces via BGP within the bounds of the parent prefix.
cloudflare_alexandria_get_application_re: An application entry in Cloudflare's Resource Library -- a catalogued real-world application identified by the hostnames, IP subnets, and port/protocol pairs its traffic matches, referenced elsewhere in Cloudflare's platform (e.g. traffic policies) by name instead of its raw network signature.
cloudflare_api_shield_public_schema_succ: An API schema registered with API Shield's schema validation feature. `source` holds the raw OpenAPI schema (JSON or YAML); once `validation_enabled`, Cloudflare validates incoming requests against it.
cloudflare_api_shield_single_operation_r: An API operation tracked by API Shield -- a specific HTTP method and endpoint template (path parameters represented as `{varN}` placeholders) on a given host, the unit API Shield's discovery, schema validation, and rate limiting features operate on.
cloudflare_app: An application registered in Cloudflare's Flagship feature-flag/experimentation platform, identified by `name`. Serves as the parent container for that application's own flags and variations.
cloudflare_asset: An asset attached to a Cloudforce One threat intelligence request -- a supporting file or artifact associated with a specific request in Cloudforce One's workflow.
cloudflare_bill_subs_api_account_subscri: An account-level billing subscription -- the paid plan or add-on component Cloudflare bills the account for, with `rate_plan` naming the plan, `component_values` any usage-based configuration, and `current_period_start`/`current_period_end` the active billing cycle.
cloudflare_bill_subs_api_payment_method_: A payment method on file for the account's billing. Cloudflare's payment-methods API supports both card and bank-transfer-style payment methods, with the bank-specific fields (routing number, account type, country) populated only for bank-based methods.
cloudflare_binding: A binding between a BYOIP address prefix (or a CIDR range within it) and a Cloudflare network service (`service_id`), directing traffic to that prefix through the bound service.
cloudflare_brand_protection_api_error: The error response shape for Brand Protection's internal submission endpoint. Discovered as a resource because the endpoint's own create and read operations share this shape; low confidence this represents a real, durable domain entity rather than an error envelope -- worth a second look against Cloudflare's own current API reference before treating as authoritative.
cloudflare_bucket: An R2 object storage bucket. `location_hint` optionally requests that new objects be stored close to a given region; `storage_class` sets the default storage class (e.g. Standard or Infrequent Access) for newly uploaded objects.
cloudflare_bulk: A bulk remediation job in Email Security's investigation tooling -- applies a single action (e.g. move, delete) across every message matching `search_params`, recording the expected disposition and an optional comment for audit purposes.
cloudflare_calls_app_response_single: A Cloudflare Calls application -- the top-level container for a WebRTC application's own SFU/TURN usage, identified by an internal `name` not shown to end users.
cloudflare_calls_turn_key_response_singl: A TURN key for Cloudflare Calls -- credentials used to authenticate to Cloudflare's TURN relay service for WebRTC NAT traversal, identified by an internal `name` not shown to end users.
cloudflare_category: A threat event category in Cloudforce One's threat intelligence platform. Classifies events against real-world threat frameworks (`mitre_attack`, `mitre_capec`) and cyber kill chain stage (`kill_chain`).
cloudflare_client_side_security_get_zone: A Page Shield policy -- defines an action Cloudflare takes against client-side scripts/connections matching a Firewall-rule-syntax `expression` on the zone, part of Page Shield's client-side security (Magecart/supply-chain attack) protection.
cloudflare_cloudforce_one_rule_preview: A structured detection rule in Cloudforce One's threat intelligence platform. `condition` holds nested match logic (up to 10 levels deep) and `content` the rule body itself; `is_public` controls whether other internal accounts can see the rule.
cloudflare_collection: A collection in Cloudforce One's threat intelligence platform -- a saved grouping of related threat intelligence items (e.g. indicators, events) for organization and sharing. Low confidence: the underlying schema carries no named fields beyond the generic response envelope, so this reading is inferred from the endpoint's own path, not from field content.
cloudflare_commit: A repository in Cloudflare's Artifacts (container registry) service, despite its own generated name -- `default_branch`, `read_only`, and `name` describe a repository, not a commit. This is a real noun-derivation mismatch in the generated type name, not a docs gap; flagged for a rename pass rather than corrected here, since this session's own scope is create-binding correctness, not noun quality.
cloudflare_config: A Hyperdrive configuration -- Cloudflare's connection-pooling and caching layer in front of an external database. `origin` defines the real database Hyperdrive connects to, `mtls` optional origin authentication, `caching` its own query-caching behavior, and `origin_connection_limit` the pool's own soft cap on origin connections.
cloudflare_cost: A custom AI provider registered with AI Gateway, despite its own generated name -- the real fields (`base_url`, `curl_example`, `js_example`, `headers`) describe a self-hosted or third-party LLM provider registration, not a cost record. A real noun-derivation mismatch (this endpoint's response schema is shared with several other generated names -- see cloudflare_custom_domain, cloudflare_custom_provider -- all really the same AI Gateway/custom-provider concept), not a docs gap.
cloudflare_crawl: A crawl job in Browser Rendering -- triggers Cloudflare's managed headless-browser service to crawl one or more pages, returning the job's own real result once complete.
cloudflare_credential: A single credential within a Vulnerability Scanner credential set -- an authentication value (e.g. API key, session token) attached to outgoing scan requests via a named header or cookie (`location`, `location_name`). `value` is write-only and never returned in API responses.
cloudflare_credential_set: A credential set in Vulnerability Scanner -- a named group of authentication credentials the scanner attaches to its own requests when authenticated scanning is needed, containing one or more individual credentials.
cloudflare_custom: A custom Data Loss Prevention (DLP) profile -- defines the detection entries, associated data classes/tags, and match-sensitivity settings (`confidence_threshold`, `allowed_match_count`, OCR/context-awareness toggles) DLP policies evaluate content against.
cloudflare_custom_domain: An AI Gateway, despite its own generated name -- Cloudflare's proxy and observability layer in front of one or more LLM providers. Configures caching (`cache_ttl`, `cache_invalidate_on_update`), authentication requirements, and logging/log-push behavior (`collect_logs`, `logpush`, `log_management`) for requests routed through the gateway. A real noun-derivation mismatch shared with several other generated names -- see cloudflare_cost, cloudflare_custom_provider.
cloudflare_custom_indicator_feeds_indica: A custom threat intelligence indicator feed registered with Cloudflare's Threat Intelligence (Intel) service -- a named, described source of indicators the account can upload and query alongside Cloudflare's own built-in feeds.
cloudflare_custom_pages_custom_asset_res: An asset (e.g. an image) used by a custom page -- referenced by name and fetched from `url`, used to brand Cloudflare's own served custom error/challenge pages.
cloudflare_custom_pages_custom_page_resu: A custom page -- Cloudflare-served HTML (e.g. a branded error or challenge page) hosted at `url`, with `state` controlling whether the custom version is active or Cloudflare's own default page is served instead.
cloudflare_custom_prompt_topic: A custom prompt topic for DLP's AI-prompt inspection -- defines a named topic (`topic`) the DLP profile `profile_id` scans AI prompts/content for, alongside Cloudflare's own built-in topics.
cloudflare_custom_provider: A custom AI provider registered with AI Gateway, the same real concept as cloudflare_cost discovered via a distinct read path in Cloudflare's own spec -- lets AI Gateway route requests to a self-hosted or third-party LLM endpoint.
cloudflare_data_class: A DLP data class -- a named detection definition (`expression`) DLP profiles reference to identify a specific category of sensitive data, with `sensitivity_levels` and associated `data_tags` used for classification and reporting.
cloudflare_data_tag: A DLP data tag within a data tag category -- a named label DLP profiles attach to matched content for classification and reporting, grouped under its parent category.
cloudflare_data_tag_category: A DLP data tag category -- a named grouping for data tags, optionally seeded from a built-in `template_id` instead of an explicit tag list.
cloudflare_database: A D1 database -- Cloudflare's managed serverless SQL database. `jurisdiction` restricts where the database runs and stores data; `primary_location_hint` requests a specific region for the primary instance; `read_replication` configures read replicas.
cloudflare_dataset: An AI Gateway, despite its own generated name -- the same real entity as cloudflare_gateway, cloudflare_cost, cloudflare_custom_domain, and cloudflare_custom_provider, all discovered from response schemas sharing the identical AI Gateway shape under different generated names. A real noun-derivation mismatch, not a docs gap.
cloudflare_deploy_hook: A deploy hook for a Cloudflare Workers Builds pipeline -- a webhook-triggered mechanism that starts a new deployment of the named branch when called, identified by its own UUID.
cloudflare_deployment: A Cloudflare Pages deployment. Built either from a git branch (`branch`, with commit metadata) or from directly uploaded files/Worker bundle (`_worker_js`/`_worker_bundle`, mutually exclusive), with `_headers`/`_redirects`/`_routes_json` as Pages' own build-time configuration files.
cloudflare_deployment_group: A deployment group for Cloudflare's Device (WARP client) management -- groups devices under a shared `version_config` and set of `policy_ids`, used to roll out WARP client versions and device policies to a defined subset of devices.
cloudflare_digital_experience_monitoring: A Digital Experience Monitoring (DEX) test -- configures the WARP client to periodically run a synthetic test (`data` holds the test's own configuration) against `target_policies`, on a recurring `interval`, for monitoring end-user network/application experience.
cloudflare_dls_prefix_binding_response: A binding between a BYOIP prefix's CIDR range and a managed region (`region_key`) in Cloudflare's Data Localization Suite -- restricts where traffic for that CIDR is processed.
cloudflare_document_fingerprint: A document fingerprint for DLP -- a hash-based detector that flags content matching a specific, previously fingerprinted document above `match_percent` similarity, rather than a pattern-based rule.
cloudflare_domain: A protected domain in Email Security's settings. Configures inbound/outbound TLS requirements, IP restrictions, and delivery/disposition handling for mail on this domain.
cloudflare_dos_dns_protection_rule_respo: A DNS Protection rule under Magic Transit's Advanced DNS Protection. Sets detection sensitivity (`burst_sensitivity`, `profile_sensitivity`, `rate_sensitivity`) and `mode` (enabled/disabled/monitoring) for a given `scope` (global, region, or datacenter), including whether to block DNS ANY queries.
cloudflare_dos_expression_filter_respons: A SYN Protection filter under Magic Transit's Advanced TCP Protection. Uses a Firewall-rule-syntax `expression` to scope which traffic the surrounding SYN Protection rules apply to, with its own independent `mode`.
cloudflare_dos_infra_prefix_response: An allowlisted prefix under Magic Transit's Advanced TCP Protection -- a CIDR range exempted from TCP-protection mitigation once `enabled`.
cloudflare_dos_prefix_response: A prefix under Magic Transit's Advanced TCP Protection -- a CIDR range that can be `excluded` from protection, distinct from cloudflare_dos_infra_prefix_response's own allowlist mechanism.
cloudflare_dos_syn_protection_rule_respo: A SYN Protection rule under Magic Transit's Advanced TCP Protection. Sets detection sensitivity, `mode`, and `mitigation_type` (challenge or retransmit) for SYN-flood mitigation at a given `scope`.
cloudflare_dos_tcp_flow_protection_rule_: A TCP Flow Protection rule under Magic Transit's Advanced TCP Protection. Sets detection sensitivity and `mode` for anomalous-TCP-flow mitigation at a given `scope`.
cloudflare_email_destination_address_res: A verified destination email address for Email Routing -- an external mailbox routing rules can forward zone email to, once the address owner confirms a verification email.
cloudflare_email_rule_response_single: An Email Routing rule for a zone. `matchers` define which incoming addresses the rule applies to and `actions` where matching mail is forwarded; `source` distinguishes rules managed via the dashboard/API/Terraform from ones managed by a Worker's own wrangler configuration.
cloudflare_email_sending_subdomain_respo: A subdomain configured for outbound Email Sending on a zone -- enables sending authenticated mail from the given subdomain (or, with the account-level wildcard feature enabled, a wildcard subdomain).
cloudflare_entry: A DLP detection entry -- a single pattern-based rule (`pattern`) attached to a DLP profile (`profile_id`), the individual detector a custom DLP profile's own `entries` list is built from.
cloudflare_evaluation: An AI Gateway, despite its own generated name -- the same real entity as cloudflare_gateway and its sibling generated names (see cloudflare_dataset's own intro for the full list). A real noun-derivation mismatch, not a docs gap.
cloudflare_event: A threat event in Cloudforce One's threat intelligence platform -- a recorded observation (attacker, target, category, indicator) within a dataset, the core unit Cloudforce One's own categories, rules, and collections organize and reference.
cloudflare_finetune_asset: A fine-tune asset for Workers AI -- a file (e.g. training data) associated with a fine-tuned model (`finetune_id`), identified within that fine-tune by `file_name`.
cloudflare_firewall_filter_response_sing: A zone-level (legacy) Firewall filter -- a reusable Firewall-rule-syntax `expression`, referenced by one or more firewall rules rather than repeating the expression inline. Superseded in newer Cloudflare accounts by the Ruleset Engine, but still live for zones on the legacy Firewall Rules product.
cloudflare_firewall_filter_rules_single_: A zone-level (legacy) Firewall rule -- pairs a `filter` (a Firewall-rule-syntax expression) with an `action` to take when matched traffic exceeds a configured threshold.
cloudflare_firewall_firewalluablock_resp: A zone-level User Agent Blocking rule (legacy Firewall product) -- blocks or challenges requests whose User-Agent header matches `configuration`, with `mode` set to a not-yet-migrated legacy shape distinct from the newer Ruleset Engine equivalent.
cloudflare_firewall_override_response_si: A zone-level WAF override (legacy Firewall product) -- adjusts the WAF's own rule behavior for requests matching the given `urls`, predating the Ruleset Engine's own per-request override mechanism.
cloudflare_firewall_ratelimit_response_s: A zone-level rate limiting rule (legacy Firewall product). Counts traffic matching `match` over a rolling `period`, applying `action` once `threshold` is exceeded within that window.
cloudflare_firewall_response_single: An account-level IP Access Rule -- allows, blocks, or challenges requests from a matched IP/IP range/country/ASN (`configuration`) across every zone on the account, with `mode` setting the action taken.
cloudflare_firewall_rule_single_response: A user-level IP Access Rule -- the same real concept as cloudflare_firewall_response_single, scoped to the authenticated user's own account context (`/user/...`) rather than an explicit account ID.
cloudflare_firewall_zonelockdown_respons: A zone-level Zone Lockdown rule (legacy Firewall product) -- restricts access to the URLs listed in `urls` so only the IP addresses/CIDR ranges in `configurations` may reach them, evaluated in `priority` order relative to other lockdown rules.
cloudflare_flag: A feature flag within a Flagship application. `default_variation` is served when the flag is off or no `rules` match; `rules` are evaluated in ascending priority order to select a different variation for matching requests.
cloudflare_gateway: An AI Gateway -- Cloudflare's proxy and observability layer in front of one or more LLM providers. Configures caching (`cache_ttl`, `cache_invalidate_on_update`), authentication requirements, and logging/log-push behavior (`collect_logs`, `logpush`, `log_management`) for requests routed through the gateway. The one correctly-named wire among a real cluster of generated-name mismatches sharing this same response shape -- see cloudflare_dataset's own intro for the full list.
cloudflare_group: A group within a Cloudforce One threat intelligence dataset -- a named collection of `members` (other dataset entities) for organizing related threat intelligence data.
cloudflare_healthchecks_single_response: A zone-level health check. Periodically probes `address` (an origin hostname or IP) from `check_regions`, tracking consecutive failures/successes against configurable thresholds before flipping the origin's own reported health status.
cloudflare_hold: A zone hold -- when set, blocks any zone activation for the hostname (e.g. via a plan change or ownership transfer) until explicitly released or, if `hold_after` is set, until that time passes. `include_subdomains` extends the same restriction to subdomains.
cloudflare_iam_response_single_account: A Cloudflare account -- the top-level billing and organizational container every zone, user, and resource belongs to. `unit` optionally places the new account under a tenant unit for multi-account (Tenant) management.
cloudflare_iam_scim_group: A SCIM Group for account-level user provisioning -- represents a group of users as defined by an external identity provider, kept in sync via the SCIM protocol; system groups (Cloudflare-managed) are distinguished from custom groups by ID prefix.
cloudflare_iam_scim_user: A SCIM User for account-level user provisioning -- represents an individual user as defined by an external identity provider (IdP), kept in sync via the SCIM protocol. `user_name` (the user's email) is the real, unique identifier; `external_id` lets the IdP track its own mapping.
cloudflare_iam_single_membership_respons: An account membership -- represents a user's own invited-or-active membership in an account. Its own real, narrow write surface is accepting or rejecting a pending invitation (`status`), not full membership management.
cloudflare_iam_sso_connector_response: An SSO connector for account-level authentication -- links a verified `email_domain` to an SSO identity provider, so users signing in with that email domain authenticate via SSO instead of a Cloudflare password. `begin_verification` starts the domain-ownership verification flow.
cloudflare_image: A Cloudflare Images image (the v1 API). Uploaded either as a direct file, from a source `url`, or referenced later via `id`; `metadata` is an arbitrary user-defined key-value store for linking the image back to an external system of record.
cloudflare_images_image_response_single: A Cloudflare Images image -- the same real concept as cloudflare_image, discovered via the images/v1 path family rather than the v1/images family (Cloudflare's own spec carries both as parallel, real API generations for the same product).
cloudflare_images_image_variant_simple_r: A Cloudflare Images variant -- a named, reusable image-resizing configuration (`options`) other parts of the platform reference by `id` (or via `variant_id`) instead of repeating resize parameters per request.
cloudflare_images_sourcingkit_migration_: A Sourcing Kit migration for Cloudflare Images -- a one-time bulk import job that copies objects from an existing external source (`source_id`, e.g. an S3-compatible bucket) into Cloudflare Images, with `conflict_behaviour`/`path_prefix`/`root_directory` controlling how the import is scoped and reconciled.
cloudflare_images_sourcingkit_source_sin: A Sourcing Kit source for Cloudflare Images -- registers an external storage bucket (`vendor`, `bucket`, `secret` credentials) as a source Sourcing Kit migrations can import from.
cloudflare_index: A Vectorize index -- Cloudflare's managed vector database. `config` defines the index's own vector dimensionality/metric; the index is the unit Workers bindings query for vector similarity search.
cloudflare_instance: An AI Search instance (formerly AutoRAG) -- Cloudflare's managed retrieval-augmented-generation pipeline. Configures the embedding model, chunking strategy (`chunk_size`, `chunk_overlap`), response caching (`cache_ttl`, `cache_threshold`), and which AI Gateway (`ai_gateway_id`) and model requests are routed through.
cloudflare_integration: A Zero Trust Risk Scoring integration -- connects an external identity/risk signal source (e.g. an Okta tenant, `tenant_url`) so its own risk signals feed into Cloudflare's device/user risk scoring.
cloudflare_intel_sinkholes_ingress_singl: An ingress rule for a Threat Intelligence sinkhole -- a BYOIP CIDR block (owned by the account) that routes matching traffic into the parent sinkhole for capture and analysis.
cloudflare_intel_sinkholes_sinkhole_sing: A Threat Intelligence sinkhole -- a managed collection endpoint for redirected malicious/suspicious traffic. Optionally stores large captured request bodies in an account-owned R2 bucket (`r2_bucket`/`r2_id`/`r2_secret`).
cloudflare_ip_profile: A Device IP profile for Zero Trust device management -- matches devices via a wirefilter `match` expression (e.g. by identity or group) and applies IP-related settings from the bound `subnet_id`, evaluated across profiles in ascending `precedence` order.
cloudflare_item: An AI Search namespace, despite its own generated name -- an isolated document collection within AI Search that a given instance searches over, distinct from cloudflare_instance itself. A real noun-derivation mismatch (the endpoint is ai-search/namespaces, not a generic 'item'), not a docs gap.
cloudflare_job: An AI Search instance, despite its own generated name -- the same real entity as cloudflare_instance, discovered via a distinct read path in Cloudflare's own spec. A real noun-derivation mismatch, not a docs gap.
cloudflare_letter: A takedown notice letter in Cloudforce One's Brand Protection service -- a generated legal notice document (`letter_text`, from `template_id`) attached to a specific takedown notice, tracking its own `letter_type`.
cloudflare_level: A sensitivity level within a DLP sensitivity group -- a named tier (e.g. low/medium/high) DLP profiles reference to weight how strongly a match should be treated.
cloudflare_lex_dataset_detail_response: A dataset registered with Logpush's Log Explorer. `dataset` names the real Cloudflare log dataset to ingest (e.g. `http_requests`); `fields`/`filter` narrow which fields and events are ingested, defaulting to everything when omitted.
cloudflare_lists_list_response_collectio: A zone/account-level list (Cloudflare's Lists product) -- a named, typed collection (`kind`: IP addresses, ASNs, hostnames, or redirects) referenced by expression in Firewall/Ruleset rules instead of enumerating values inline.
cloudflare_load_balancing_monitor_group_: A Load Balancing monitor group -- groups several individual health-check monitors (`members`) so a load balancer pool can reference the group instead of a single monitor, treating pool health as the aggregate of the group's own monitors.
